recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future implementation behavior changes should be handled in the IG Publisher/tooling repository or its documentation unless a later work-group decision changes the core guide-parameter-code definition.
issue_request: FHIR-12523 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR Infrastructure change request from the DSTU2 cycle asking for broken links in generated documentation to cause at least build warnings and to be preventable once known broken links were fixed. The resolution was to add capability for editors to manage this better.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN r11983, now git commit 64e060603fc58a5b7794f2d4e696796817b3faaf, which changed the then-in-tree IG publisher so a control-file broken-links setting of error halted the build when broken links were found. Later source refactors preserved the behavior's editor-facing representation as the ImplementationGuide guide parameter code rule-broken-links.
additional_context: ImplementationGuide is active in source/fhir.ini and ImplementationGuide.definition.parameter.code is bound to ValueSet/guide-parameter-code. The current CodeSystem source defines rule-broken-links with warning/error values and default error semantics. The old Java publisher implementation is no longer in this FHIR checkout, and Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no later decision reversing or narrowing the applied tracker.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scoped core source already documents the requested editor-facing broken-link control, and duplicate prose or generated-history edits would not change implementer understanding.
